description:
Implements the three UI-state hooks that give Filament components local, ephemeral state: use_state, use_memo, and use_effect. These hooks are SERVER-SIDE equivalents of React hooks — they run during the component render pass on the LiveView process, store state in the fiber tree, and trigger re-renders by messaging the owning LiveView process.

TRACK C ONLY COVERS UI STATE. Domain state (GenServer observations) is Track D.

## Prerequisites — Track B must be fully merged before any C ticket begins

Track B delivers these files (DO NOT recreate them — modify in place):
  lib/filament/fiber.ex           — %Filament.Fiber{} struct
  lib/filament/vnode.ex           — VNode IR types
  lib/filament/component.ex       — defcomponent macro, Filament.Component behaviour
  lib/filament/sigil_f.ex         — ~F sigil
  lib/filament/html_engine.ex     — Filament.HTMLEngine tag handler
  lib/filament/render_context.ex  — %Filament.RenderContext{}
  lib/filament/renderer.ex        — Filament.Renderer.render/3
  lib/filament/reconciler.ex      — Filament.Reconciler (mount/2, update/3, unmount/1)
  lib/filament/reconciler_error.ex
  lib/filament/live_view.ex       — Filament.LiveView adapter (use Filament.LiveView)
  test/support/fixtures/          — HelloComponent, WrapperComponent, CounterComponent, ParentComponent

## Project root
/Users/j5n/Workspace/filament/filament/

## Key LiveView API used in this track
  attach_hook(socket, :filament_effects, :after_render, fn socket -> socket end)
  Attaches a lifecycle hook. The function receives and must return the socket.
  Available since phoenix_live_view 0.20. Confirmed present in ~> 1.0.
  Source: deps/phoenix_live_view/lib/phoenix_live_view/lifecycle.ex

## The hooks rules (document in Filament.Hooks moduledoc)
  1. Only call hooks at the top level of render/1 — never inside conditionals or loops.
  2. Only call hooks during a component render pass — never in event handlers or effect bodies.
  3. Hooks are identified by call ORDER. The same hook called in the same position always
     receives the same slot index. Violating rule 1 shifts all subsequent indices.
  Track C does not enforce these rules at runtime (deferred). They are documented and trusted.

## Delivery order
  C1 (slot infrastructure) → C2 (use_state) and C3 (use_memo) in parallel → C4 (use_effect)

## Deviation policy
  Any deviation from a ticket's spec requires prior approval. Stop work, run
  'bw comment <id> "..."' describing the conflict, set the ticket back to open with
  'bw reopen <id>', and await guidance. Do not improvise.
